claims.claim: The vita activa is designated by three fundamental human activities: labor, work, and action, each corresponding to a basic condition under which human life on earth is given.
qualifications: limited to labor, work, and action
claims.supporting_excerpt: With the term vita activa , I propose to designate three fundamental human activities: labor, work, and action. They are fundamental because each corresponds to one of the basic conditions under which life on earth has been given to man.

claims.claim: Men are fundamentally conditioned beings because everything they contact and all human-made things turn immediately into a condition of their existence.
qualifications: applies to whatever touches or enters into a sustained relationship with human life
claims.supporting_excerpt: Men are conditioned beings because everything they come in contact with turns immediately into a condition of their existence.

definitions.definition: The activity corresponding to the biological process of the human body, bound to vital necessities, where the human condition of labor is life itself.

The activity corresponding to the unnaturalness of human existence, providing an artificial world of things meant to outlast and transcend individuals, where the human condition of work is worldliness.
The only activity going on directly between men without intermediaries, corresponding to the human condition of plurality.

distinctions.distinction: Labor corresponds to the biological life process and body, whereas work corresponds to the unnaturalness of human existence and creates an artificial world of things distinct from natural surroundings.

must_not_be_lost: The connection between labor, work, action and natality versus mortality.
The characterization of plurality as the condition of human action.
parsed.segment_function: Definition and phenomenological analysis of the vita activa (labor, work, and action) and its corresponding human conditions.
